transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer technical support, my name is Ryan. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Ryan. Our broadband went completely dead about twenty minutes ago! The council is doing emergency water pipe repairs down our road and their digger literally just ripped through the cables under the pavement!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand how alarming that is, Benjamin, especially seeing physical construction machinery damage the cables right outside your house. Let me check the local network status immediately.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks Ryan. The broadband light turned solid red immediately when the digger struck the duct.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we pull up the regional infrastructure telemetry, Benjamin, could you please verify your installation address and your four-digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 14 Mill Lane, Cambridge, CB2 1RX, and the security PIN is 7402.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for verifying those details, Benjamin. I have your full fibre optical connection open on our monitoring console.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, thanks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to confirm what has occurred: council contractors carrying out water main roadworks on Mill Lane have severed the underground telecoms duct, causing an immediate total loss of broadband service with a solid red LOS light on your optical ONT. Is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly that. All the neighbors on our side of the street came outside because everyone lost internet at the exact same moment.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Checking our optical line terminal telemetry for the Cambridge exchange... yes, an optical loss of signal alarm triggered twenty-four minutes ago affecting forty-two premises on Mill Lane.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you see the exact break point from your exchange console?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our automated optical time-domain reflectometer indicates an optical fiber break at six hundred and forty meters from the distribution node, which aligns with your street location.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The water utility workers have stopped digging now and they're looking into the trench.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because this involves physical duct and fiber severing by a third party, Openreach civil engineering and fiber splicing teams must be deployed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How long will an emergency fiber splice like that take to repair?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The priority major service outage ticket has already been dispatched under incident reference MSO-49102.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is Openreach already on their way out to the site?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: An emergency response civil engineering crew has been dispatched from the regional depot with an estimated arrival time of ninety minutes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's relatively quick for an emergency crew to mobilize.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Once the civil team clears the debris and rodded ducting, optical engineers will pull through a replacement seventy-two-core fiber cable.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Do they have to fuse each individual fiber glass core by hand?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, technicians use high-precision fusion splicers inside an all-weather splicing vehicle to join each ribbon pair.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What is the expected timeline for getting forty-two homes back online?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The target restoration window for this class of civil infrastructure damage is twelve to eighteen hours.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Twelve to eighteen hours?! I run a medical consulting practice from home and I have telemedicine clinics booked all day tomorrow! Losing eighteen hours of internet will completely destroy my schedule, this is a total disaster!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand how critical this is for your medical telemedicine appointments, Benjamin. Let me look at our emergency mobile backup options for you right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Ryan, because I cannot cancel those patient appointments.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We can activate an immediate emergency unlimited mobile data tethering bolt-on for your S-Net mobile plan free of charge.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I do have an S-Net mobile SIM card in my iPad and personal phone.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What is the mobile number on your personal S-Net handset?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The mobile number is zero seven seven zero zero, nine zero zero six four one.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please bear with me while I place you on a brief hold for about one minute while I apply the emergency unlimited data bolt-on to that number.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience while holding, Benjamin. The unlimited high-speed data bolt-on has been applied to zero seven seven zero zero, nine zero zero six four one.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Ryan. How fast can I hotspot my laptop to my phone?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Cambridge has full 5G ultra-wideband coverage, so your tethered hotspot will provide between one hundred and two hundred megabits download.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is more than enough speed to host multi-party video consultations.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can also connect your home desktop to your phone hotspot via Wi-Fi or USB tethering.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'll use USB tethering to keep the phone charged while transmitting video.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You will also receive automated SMS updates every four hours tracking the Openreach civil excavation and fiber splicing progress.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will keep me posted without needing to call back.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And under our service level agreement, auto-compensation credits will apply for the outage duration.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the council roadworks contractor have financial liability for damaging the Openreach ducting?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Openreach's third-party damage recovery unit will bill the municipal utility contractor directly for all civil excavation and fiber splicing labor costs.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good, because they shouldn't dig without checking subterranean utility maps first.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: All contractors are required to request statutory undertaker plant drawings before using mechanical excavators.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will our optical ONT box need to be power cycled once the physical glass is spliced back together?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The ONT will automatically detect optical laser carrier sync and negotiate a GPON link within sixty seconds of splice completion.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And does the LOS red light turn off on its own?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the red LOS alarm extinguishes and the green PON light turns solid once the optical power margin reaches minus nineteen dBm.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What should I do if the PON light is still flashing tomorrow morning?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If the PON indicator flashes green, it indicates ranging negotiation, which resolves within three minutes once exchange registration finishes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's very helpful technical guidance so I don't panic if it blinks briefly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our automated network management system will also dispatch a completion SMS to zero seven seven zero zero, nine zero zero six four one.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will notify me the moment the street fiber is live.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And your 5G unlimited tethering allowance will remain active for seven full days so you have plenty of buffer.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Having seven days of unlimited 5G backup gives me immense peace of mind for the practice.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How will the excavation team ensure safety around the open pavement trench overnight?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The contractors install rigid interlocking pedestrian barriers and road safety boarding around the trench perimeter.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's good, so neighborhood children and pets don't wander near the exposed cables.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Alright, the major incident ticket is logged under MSO-49102. Have a good day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will all promotional discounts and package bundles remain completely protected throughout the network repair?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, all contract discounts and promotional bundles remain fully active and protected on your billing profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, Ryan, will my direct debit discount remain intact during the outage?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, bill credits apply automatically. Thank you for choosing S-Net today, Benjamin. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks Ryan, goodbye.
